# audit: gap-mapped children re-screen in-main-slot and overwrite serviced child audits

## Observed on SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB (epic, all 10 children terminal and on dev)

An epic audit whose **parent** carries one `partial` AC cannot converge while the
default in-main-slot child-audit mode is active. Every run re-screens the same
gap-mapped children, re-blocks on the pending-screens gate, and (worse) overwrites
child audits that a previous session had serviced with real verdicts.

## Root cause (two interacting behaviours)

1. **Gap-mapped children ignore their stored verdict.** In the default
   parent-first flow (`_phase_children`, `audit_children=False`) the
   `not parent_gaps` branch consults `_child_content_changed()` (content-gated
   reuse), but the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch appends the child
   to `pending_children` **without** consulting its stored audit — unlike the
   `--audit-children` P7 pre-pass, which reuses a fresh stored child audit via
   `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and never re-screens it.
2. **In-main-slot mode cannot service screens inside the run.** With
   `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` (default `true`) the gap-mapped child screens are
   emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` and the child audits are persisted as
   `partial` + `main-session review`. A later `persist` pass then **overwrites**
   the previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit with that pending
   `partial` report.

Net effect: service the screens → re-run the parent → the children are re-screened
and their good audits are destroyed → the parent still reports
`Ready to close: No` with `Child screens pending`. The
`<id>.pending-screens.json` signal is never cleared.

## Evidence (this item's run)

| Step | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Audit run 1 | 08:13 | `Ready to close: No`, 7 in-main-slot screens emitted |
| Screens serviced by the session (real file:line evidence) | ~09:55 | 6 children `Yes`, 1 `No` (documented downstream AC) |
| Audit re-run (`--force`, because the stored report was content-fresh) | 10:04 | 14 screens re-emitted; **all 7 child audits overwritten back to `partial` + `main-session review`**; parent `No` with 7 pending screens |
| Screens re-serviced by hand (again) | 10:20 | 6 `Yes` / 1 `No` restored |

The parent's single blocking AC (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB AC10) is a downstream
verification owned by a **different repository** (`LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X`), so it can
never become `met` on this host — the loop is permanent, not a transient state.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow, a
  gap-mapped child with a content-fresh stored audit is reused (its persisted AC
  verdicts adopted, exactly as the `--audit-children` pre-pass does) and is NOT
  added to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run never persists a
  pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and
  carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** With all children terminal and only one unsatisfiable
  parent AC, a re-run after servicing the child screens reports
  `Ready to close: No` naming **that AC only** (no `Child screens pending` gate),
  and the pending-screens signal is cleared.
- **AC4 — Regression tests** cover both flows (gap-mapped reuse, no overwrite on
  persist) with no real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this (discovered-from).
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling
  (mitigates the reporting side only; it does not stop the re-screen/overwrite).
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — the cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent
  permanently `partial` on this host.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** – Audit: parent-first child pass-through (audit parent only first) (completed)
- **SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM** – Re-resolve pending children on checkpoint resume (completed)
- **SA-0MU32TE120012T49** – R5: Enforce the child-audit execution contract (no silent pending child screens) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvawfuu0004vw45, 0mvawfyze0040sq3, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+139 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvawfuu0004vw45, 0mvawfyze0040sq3, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+133 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+129 more)

# audit_runner false-positive chore deduplication and needsProducerReview fix

## Problem

Every `audit_runner.py issue <id>` run that finds a medium/low severity code-quality finding classified as *candidate false positive* creates a **new** chore work item on every audit cycle. Combined with the runner's behaviour of setting `needsProducerReview = true` on every passing (`Ready to close: Yes`) top-level audit (when a prior passing audit with an identical v2 content fingerprint does not already exist), this means:

1. A backlog of 20+ duplicate chore items accumulates (same ruff rule in same file, re-created every audit run).
2. 7 of 36 in_review items on the 2026-11-02 release were blocked purely because the producer-review gate found `needsProducerReview` set by these chores — clearing the flag is manual, and the next audit re-arms it.
3. Releases cannot converge: each audit creates new chores, and each passing audit re-sets the flag.

The chore-creation path (lines ~12061–12080 in `audit_runner.py`) does **no deduplication**: it iterates `fp_screen_results` and creates a new chore for every medium/low `confident-false-positive` entry regardless of whether an identical chore already exists.

## Users

- **Release operator** — wants `/skill:ship release` to succeed without manually clearing `needsProducerReview` flags on dozens of false-positive chores.
- **Producer (Map)** — does not need to make a decision on every lint false positive every audit cycle; wants a one-time suppression mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeated audits of the same unchanged item do not create duplicate chore items — deduplicated by rule code + file path + line number + content fingerprint; proven by a test.
2. An audit ending `Ready to close: Yes` does **not** set `needsProducerReview` when the only medium/low false-positive candidate chores are already tracked (no new chores created means no flag set).
3. An accepted false positive can be recorded once (via `auditWaiver` on the parent item) and no longer triggers chore creation or flag-setting for that rule+file+line combination.
4. Release gate regression test: a repository with N accepted false-positive chores does not fail the ship producer-review gate.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Blocks `/skill:ship release` on repositories with deliberate lint patterns; each release needs manual flag clearing (2026-11-02 release: 7 items cleared by hand).

## Constraints

- Must preserve the existing `confident-false-positive` remediation path for critical/high findings (that path triggers config fixes and commits — untouched).
- Must preserve `uncertain` and `genuine` findings as blocking (no behavioural change for non-false-positives).
- `auditWaiver` field already exists on work items and can be extended for this purpose.
- Deduplication must be idempotent across audit runs — running twice in a row must yield the same chore set.

## Existing state

- `_create_chore_item()` (line 11837) creates a chore for every medium/low `confident-false-positive` finding without checking for duplicates.
- `_producer_review_required_reason()` and the lifecycle code at line ~14769 set `needsProducerReview` on every passing top-level audit unless a prior passing audit with an identical v2 content fingerprint is found.
- Medium/low CFPs are **not remediable** (they skip the config-fix loop) but are **treated as blocking** via `_has_phase1_blocking_issues` — they never block because they are excluded from the `cq_findings` severity check, but the `needsProducerReview` flag is still set on passing audits because the runner's logic does not distinguish "only medium/low CFPs present" from "genuine blocking issues".
- `auditWaiver` field exists on work items (currently `null`).

## Desired change

1. **Deduplication layer**: Before creating a chore, check whether a chore for this exact finding (rule+file+line) already exists. Use a `seen` set keyed by `rule:file:line` within the run, and prefer reusing an existing chore rather than creating a new one.
2. **Flag gating**: In the producer-review decision, when the audit passes (`Ready to close: Yes`) and the only medium/low findings are CFPs with tracking chores, do **not** set `needsProducerReview`. The flag should only be set when there is a genuine producer decision required (uncertain findings, genuine critical/high findings, or content changes).
3. **Waiver storage**: When a producer reviews and accepts a false positive, record the waiver on the parent item's `auditWaiver` field (a list of `{rule, file, line, justification, auditedAt}`). A waived finding is excluded from chore creation and from blocking checks.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing the chore-creation logic could affect downstream consumers
  that rely on one chore per finding (e.g. dashboards, reports). **Mitigation:**
  chore IDs are preserved when reusing; the audit report still records all
  findings with their classifications — only duplicate *creation* is prevented.
- **Risk:** Deduplication by rule+file+line may be too coarse if the same line
  carries multiple ruff findings for the same rule. **Mitigation:** add the
  finding message to the key if needed.
- **Assumption:** The `auditWaiver` field on work items can accept an array of
  waiver objects. Verified by inspecting the worklog schema — `auditWaiver` is
  a nullable field; extending it to a list is safe.
- **Scope:** A producer-facing UI for waivers is out of scope. The mechanism
  is data-level only (wl update --audit-waiver or programmatic).
- **Scope creep:** This item does NOT change the remediation path for
  critical/high `confident-false-positive` findings — those continue to
  trigger config fixes and commits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — main implementation changes
  - `_create_chore_item()` — add deduplication check
  - `_run_remediation_loop()` — add waiver-based filtering and deduplication
  - `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` — consider waivers
  - `_resolve_producer_review_decision()` — gate flag on "only tracked CFPs"
  - `_producer_review_preserved()` — extend to check waiver state
- `skill/audit/tests/` — new tests for deduplication, waiver, and flag-gating behaviour
- `command/` / `skill/ship/` — verify the ship gate respects waivers

## Related work

- SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR — Audit: on ruff false positive, fix the ruff config and re-run (completed)
- SA-0MST01NPD007MYG4 — Tests: false-positive screen (ruff findings) (completed)
- SA-0MST01O4G002VPBR — False-positive screen (audit Phase 1) (completed)
- SA-0MST01OX4007Z17C — Config remediation loop (ruff false positives) (completed)
- SA-0MSYPAV1R000SMHK — Bug: audit false-positive screen crashes (completed)
- SA-0MW548R9Z0012N44, SA-0MW3G6LWN009A9UY, SA-0MW529FKC009MURB, ... — Duplicate chore items currently open (examples of the problem)
data.title: audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every medium/low 'candidate false positive' chore, blocking releases

## Problem statement

The tracked `.pi-config/agent/models.json` MunitoAI provider lists only `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`. The MunitoAI API serves two DeepSeek models, and the operator wants the newer `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` also available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/models.json` exposes both paid MunitoAI DeepSeek models under one `MunitoAI` provider — `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` (existing) and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (new) — with `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`; no credential is committed.
- [ ] Both models share the same limits: `contextWindow: 400000`, `maxTokens: 16384`, `input: ["text"]`, `api: "openai-completions"`.
- [ ] The unverified limits for the new model are flagged as unverified (see note below).
- [ ] Tracked JSON formatting and indentation are preserved.

## Note on "flagged as unverified"

JSON has no comment syntax, so the "code comment" flag cannot live inside `models.json`. The flag is recorded in `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` (docstring/constant above the MunitoAI refresh) and in `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`. This resolution is an assumption; if the operator insists on an in-file marker, a non-standard `//` comment would make the file invalid JSON and is rejected.

## Key Files

- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — add one entry to the MunitoAI models array

## Constraints

- Pure data change — no code or tests.
data.title: Update tracked models.json to add DeepSeek v4.1-flash-1017 to MunitoAI provider

## Goal

Implement the `--strict` / `--no-strict` CLI flags and `AUDIT_STRICT` env var. Thread `strict: bool` through `_AuditContext` to the F3 path, the merge gate, the report assembler, and the `--json` payload.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `audit_runner.py issue --strict` sets `strict=True`; `--no-strict` sets `strict=False`; default is `strict=False` (permissive).
2. `AUDIT_STRICT=1` env var sets `strict=True` when no flag overrides.
3. Precedence: flag > env > default, resolved once at launch and recorded.
4. `strict` is a field on `_AuditContext`, threaded to all consumers.
5. `audit_runner.py batch` subcommand also accepts `--strict` / `--no-strict`.
6. The resolved mode is recorded in the report (`## Test Failure Mode` section) and `--json` payload (`test_failure_mode` key).
7. Strict mode reproduces today's verdict for a red suite (any failure ⇒ blocked).
8. Unit tests pass (see child test items).

## Deliverables
- Argparse additions: `--strict` (store_true), `--no-strict` (store_false), `--strict` overrides env
- `_AuditContext.strict: bool` field, resolved in `cmd_issue`
- Report: `## Test Failure Mode` section header
- `--json` payload: `test_failure_mode: "strict" | "permissive"`

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (argparse section, `_AuditContext`, `cmd_issue`, report assembly, `--json` payload)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
- `command/audit.md` (optional, if prompt enumerates flags)

## Goal

Implement the failure classification and relatedness helper functions in `audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` returns `"unit"` or `"integration"`:
   - Path convention: `tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` → `integration`
   - Everything else → `unit`
   - Unclassifiable (no path data) → `integration` (fail closed)

2. `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` returns `"affected"`, `"unrelated"`, or `"inconclusive"`:
   - Test file path ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Module imported by test file ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Changed file is shared test infrastructure (`conftest.py`, `tests/helpers/**`) → `affected`
   - No match → `inconclusive`

3. `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` returns per-failure verdicts:
   - Creates scratch worktree at baseline commit (pre-change commit)
   - Runs only inconclusive failures through `paced_runner()` under `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down
   - Identical failure → `unrelated`; Pass → `affected`
   - Any baseline failure → `affected` (fail closed)
   - Any baseline error (worktree add, merge-base unresolvable, test absent) → `affected` (fail closed, no crash)
   - Never executes the main checkout; never recurses into nested suite runs

4. Scope classification and relatedness algorithm: failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.

5. No real suite execution in unit tests (mock `paced_runner` / subprocess)
6. Unit tests pass (see child test items)

## Deliverables
- `_classify_test_failure_scope()` — path-pattern classifier
- `_failure_relatedness()` — deterministic mapping + import scan
- `_baseline_unrelated()` — scratch worktree baseline re-run
- Error handling: never crashes, always returns `affected` for infrastructure failures

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (new functions)
data.title: Feature: failure classification and relatedness module

# Acquire per-child lock in phase_drive before spawning the session

## Problem

`phase_start` acquires and releases the per-child lock during its short-lived
subprocess. When `phase_drive` runs `parent` (which runs `start` as a
subprocess), the lock is acquired and released within that subprocess, leaving
a gap: the lock file's recorded pid is the dead start subprocess pid, and
no kernel flock exists while the driven child session is alive. The hydrator
therefore demotes the child to `open`.

## Fix

In `phase_drive` (implement.py), after `parent` returns with a `next_child`
and a worktree, acquire the per-child lock before spawning the session and
release it after the session exits (in a finally block). This ensures:

1. The lock file's recorded pid is the live driver pid (satisfies AC1).
2. The kernel flock is held for the session's whole lifetime (satisfies AC1).
3. `_child_session_env()` already picks up the token from `_child_lock_global`
   (set via `_set_child_lock(lock)`), so the token propagates to the spawned
   session (satisfies AC2).
4. The session's `start`/`finish` subprocesses re-enter the lock by token
   (already implemented in WorkItemLock, tested in existing suite).
5. A different live owner is still refused: the lock.acquire() returns
   acquired=False if another holder exists, and the driver should report
   skipped-held (satisfies AC4).

## Key code changes in phase_drive

After resolving child_id and worktree_path (around line 16410), before
calling spawner:

    Acquire the per-child lock for this child before spawning the session.
    lock = _new_child_lock(child_id)
    lock_result = lock.acquire()

    if not lock_result.acquired:
        # Another live holder: report skipped-held and don't spawn.
        report["action"] = ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD
        report["skipped_held"] = True
        ...
        break

    _set_child_lock(lock)
    try:
        env = _child_session_env(worktree_path=worktree_path)
        # env now includes IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN from _child_lock_global
        spawn_result = spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env)
    finally:
        _release_child_lock()

The existing start subprocess (invoked by parent) runs before this point
and acquires/releases the lock itself - no change needed there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The lock file's pid is the driver process (live), and a kernel
  flock is held while the session runs.
- AC2: `_child_session_env()` returns an env with
  `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` set to the driver's lock token, and the
  spawned session's start/finish re-enter without error.
- AC3: The lock is released in a finally block - it is released on
  success, non-zero exit, and timeout.
- AC4: If the lock is already held by a different live owner, the driver
  reports skipped-held and spawns no session.
- AC5: Existing tests (`test_phase_start_child_lock.py`,
  `test_drive_child_lock.py`, `test_drive_child_session.py`) stay green.

## Related

Parent: SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR
data.title: phase_drive acquires child lock before spawning session and releases after exit
